key_insight: HarmQ shows that quantum neural networks can be backdoored with harmonic, low-frequency triggers that survive downsampling and align with quantum circuit spectral bias.
engineering_relevance: For practical QNN deployment, this highlights a security risk unique to NISQ-era models and suggests trigger robustness must be considered alongside accuracy.
method: Use coarse-grid, block-uniform patterns to survive aggressive downsampling
Exploit parameterized quantum circuits’ preference for Fourier-like, low-frequency features
evidence_signal: On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, HarmQ reports over 99% attack success rate while preserving more than 90% clean accuracy, outperforming prior methods by a wide margin.
watch_item: Results are shown on benchmark datasets and black-box training-data access; real hardware noise, different preprocessing pipelines, and cross-dataset transfer may affect effectiveness.
paper_title: HarmQ: Harmonic Backdoor Attacks Against Quantum Neural Networks
